q: What is a contract?
r: A legally enforceable agreement between two or more parties
It needs an offer, acceptance and consideration.
w: A casual promise between friends that has no legal weight
A list of rules posted on the wall of a business
A report of a company's earnings for the year

q: What is consideration in a contract?
r: Something of value that each party gives to the other
It can be money, goods, services or a promise.
w: The time a party spends thinking about the agreement
A polite gesture shown by one side to the other
The fee paid to a court to register the contract

q: Which person generally cannot be held to most contracts?
r: A minor
Minors can usually cancel most contracts.
w: A business owner who is an adult of sound mind
A manager who signed with full knowledge
A customer who read every term

q: What is a breach of contract?
r: Failing to carry out a duty required by the agreement
The other side may seek a remedy.
w: Carrying out every duty on the agreed date
Asking a lawyer to review the agreement

q: A vendor agrees to deliver 500 chairs by June 1 but delivers 300 on June 15. What is this?
r: A breach of contract
The vendor failed to perform as agreed.
w: A valid change in the contract

q: What is a warranty?
r: A promise about the quality or performance of a product
Buyers can seek a remedy if it is broken.
w: A tax collected on each sale
A fee charged for returning a product

q: What is the main purpose of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC)?
r: To make laws for sales of goods more consistent among states
Businesses can rely on similar rules.
w: To set the tax rate on every sale of goods
To control the hiring and firing of workers
To replace the need for written contracts

q: What is negligence?
r: Failing to use reasonable care, causing harm to another
It can lead to a civil lawsuit.
w: Deliberately harming another person for gain

q: A store ignores a spill for an hour and a customer slips and is hurt. Which legal concept applies?
r: Negligence
The store failed to take reasonable care.

q: What is a patent?
r: Exclusive rights to an invention for a set time
It rewards innovation.
w: Exclusive rights to a brand name or logo
Exclusive rights to a book or song

q: What is a copyright?
r: Legal protection for original creative works
It covers books, music, art and software.

q: A band writes an original song. Which protection applies automatically to the song?
r: Copyright
It protects original creative works.
w: That allows a business to operate.

q: What is limited liability?
r: Owners are not personally responsible for business debts beyond their investment
Corporations and LLCs offer it.
w: Owners are fully responsible for all business debts
Owners are exempt from all taxes

q: Which business form gives the owner unlimited personal liability?
r: A sole proprietorship
The owner and business are legally the same.

q: What is an at-will employment relationship?
r: Either side may end the job at any time for any lawful reason
Illegal reasons are still prohibited.
w: Employees can be fired only after a written warning
Employees must give a year's notice before leaving
Employers must provide a reason for every firing

q: What does the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) require of employers?
r: Reasonable accommodations for qualified workers with disabilities
It bars disability discrimination.
w: Paying workers with disabilities more than others
It does not require higher pay.

q: What is antitrust law designed to do?
r: Promote competition and prevent unfair monopolies
It bans price fixing.

q: Two rival gas stations secretly agree to charge the same high price. Which law is most likely broken?
r: Antitrust law against price fixing
Competitors may not set prices together.

q: What is a communication barrier?
r: Something that blocks a message from being understood
Jargon and noise are examples.
w: A tool that makes messages clearer
A rule that requires messages to be short

q: What is feedback in communication?
r: The receiver's response that shows how the message was understood
It completes the communication loop.
w: The first words a sender says
The channel used to send a message
A written copy of the message

q: What is active listening?
r: Fully focusing on the speaker and responding thoughtfully
It includes paraphrasing.
w: Waiting for your turn to talk
Interrupting to share your own view
Looking at your phone while someone talks

q: A customer explains a problem and the employee restates it to confirm understanding. Which skill is this?
r: Paraphrasing as part of active listening
It checks that the message was understood.

q: What is nonverbal communication?
r: Messages sent through body language, tone and facial expression
It often shows feelings.
w: Messages sent in spoken words only

q: A speaker says she is excited but looks at the floor with crossed arms. What message does the audience likely receive?
r: Mixed signals because body language clashes with the words
People trust nonverbal cues.

q: Which channel is best for sharing a policy change with 200 employees at once?
r: A company-wide email or announcement
It reaches everyone and leaves a record.
w: A private talk with each person
A single phone call to one supervisor

q: What is the purpose of an agenda?
r: To list the topics to be covered in a meeting
It keeps the meeting focused.
w: To record what happened in a past meeting
To list every attendee's job title

q: What are meeting minutes?
r: The official written record of what happened in a meeting
They list decisions and actions.
w: The length of time a meeting lasts
A list of topics for a future meeting

q: Why should business writing be concise?
r: Readers can understand the message quickly
Brief writing saves time.
w: Longer messages are always more polite
Short messages hide the real meaning

q: Which email subject line is best?
r: Meeting moved to Thursday at 2 p.m.
It is clear and specific.
w: Please read this immediately or else

q: What is the best way to deliver bad news to a customer?
r: Be honest, respectful and offer next steps
Direct, kind messages preserve trust.
w: Hide it inside a long message of unrelated details
Send it late at night without explanation

q: What is jargon?
r: Specialized words that outsiders may not understand
It can confuse customers.
w: A greeting at the start of a call

q: A technician uses technical terms with a customer who looks confused. What should the technician do?
r: Explain again in plain language
Clear language helps understanding.
w: Ignore the confusion and move on

q: What is persuasion?
r: Influencing others to accept an idea or take action
Good persuasion uses reasons and evidence.
w: Forcing others to obey without choice

q: What does tone mean in writing?
r: The writer's attitude shown through word choice
It can be formal or friendly.
w: The font used in a document

q: What is a customer service standard?
r: A set expectation for how customers should be treated
Standards keep service consistent.
w: A price that a customer pays
A discount offered once a year

q: A hotel promises check-in within 5 minutes. A guest waits 20. What should staff do?
r: Apologize, fix the problem and offer a small gesture
Recovery builds loyalty.
w: Tell the guest the wait was normal
Blame the guest for arriving early

q: What is a customer complaint?
r: A statement that a product or service did not meet expectations
It is useful feedback.
w: A request for a store's hours

q: Which response best handles an upset customer?
r: Listen without interrupting and offer a solution
It shows respect and resolves the issue.
w: Argue to prove the customer is wrong
Tell the customer to calm down and walk away

q: What is customer retention?
r: Keeping existing customers over time
Retained customers buy again.

q: Why is it often cheaper to keep a customer than to win a new one?
r: New customers cost more to attract through marketing
Existing customers already know the brand.
w: New customers always pay higher prices

q: What is a customer survey used for?
r: Learning customers' opinions and satisfaction
It guides improvements.

q: What is a loyalty program?
r: A program that rewards customers for repeat purchases
Points and perks bring customers back.
w: A program that charges customers extra fees
A program that limits the products customers can see
That is not a loyalty program.
A program that removes customer feedback
That is not a loyalty program.

q: A coffee shop gives a free drink after ten purchases. What is the main goal?
r: Encourage repeat visits
Rewards build loyalty.
w: Reduce its costs on every sale
Prevent customers from buying other items

q: What does empathy mean when serving customers?
r: Understanding and acknowledging how the customer feels
It builds trust.
w: Agreeing with every demand a customer makes
Ignoring emotions to focus on rules

q: A customer's order arrives late for a birthday party. Which response shows empathy?
r: I'm sorry this affected your party, let me fix it right away
It acknowledges the feeling and acts.
w: Delays happen all the time, it is not a big deal
There is nothing I can do

q: What is a surplus?
r: When quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded
Prices tend to fall.
w: When quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied
When supply and demand are equal
When a firm earns a profit

q: What is a shortage?
r: When quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied
Prices tend to rise.
w: When quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded
When supply and demand are equal
When a firm has too many workers

q: A new video game console sells out within minutes at its list price. What does this suggest?
r: Demand exceeds supply at that price
A shortage exists.
w: Supply exceeds demand at that price
The price is too high for buyers

q: What is elasticity of demand?
r: How much quantity demanded changes when price changes
Elastic goods are sensitive to price.
w: How quickly a product is delivered
How much a product costs to make
How many stores sell a product

q: Which good tends to have inelastic demand?
r: Insulin for a patient with diabetes
There is no close substitute.

q: What is gross domestic product (GDP)?
r: The total value of goods and services produced in a country
It measures economic output.
w: The total money held by the government

q: What is inflation?
r: A general rise in prices over time
Money buys less.
w: A rise in the price of one item
A rise in the number of jobs

q: Prices rise 4 percent while a worker's pay rises 2 percent. What happens to purchasing power?
r: It falls
Prices grew faster than pay.

q: What is unemployment?
r: Being without a job while actively seeking work
It is measured as a rate.

q: What is fiscal policy?
r: Government decisions about taxes and spending
Congress and the president set it.
w: Central bank decisions about interest rates

q: What is monetary policy?
r: Central bank actions that influence interest rates and money supply
The Federal Reserve sets it.
w: Government decisions about taxes and spending

q: To slow rapidly rising inflation, the Federal Reserve is most likely to:
r: Raise interest rates
Higher rates cool spending.
w: The Fed does not set taxes.

q: What is a monopoly?
r: A market with a single seller and no close substitutes
The seller has strong price control.
w: A market with many equal sellers

q: What is a trade deficit?
r: When a country imports more than it exports
Imports exceed exports in value.
w: When a country exports more than it imports
When a government spends more than it collects
When a country stops all trade

q: A country exports $300 billion and imports $340 billion. What is its trade balance?
r: A deficit of $40 billion
$300 billion minus $340 billion equals -$40 billion.

q: What is self-regulation?
r: Managing your emotions and impulses in healthy ways
It helps you respond calmly.

q: A worker receives harsh criticism and pauses before replying calmly. Which skill is this?
r: Self-regulation
Managing emotion before reacting.

q: What is social awareness?
r: Recognizing and understanding other people's emotions
It supports teamwork.

q: What is relationship management?
r: Building and keeping positive relationships with others
It includes communication and conflict resolution.

q: Two teammates disagree. A third listens to both and suggests a compromise. Which skill is she using?
r: Conflict management
She helps resolve the disagreement.
w: She did not try to win.

q: What is stress management?
r: Using healthy strategies to handle pressure
Exercise and planning help.
w: Taking on more work to feel busy

q: Which action best reduces workplace stress?
r: Prioritizing tasks and taking short breaks
These habits lower overload.
w: Ignoring deadlines until the last day

q: What is resilience?
r: The ability to recover from setbacks and adapt
Resilient people try again.
w: Giving up when things get hard

q: A salesperson loses a big deal and decides to learn from it and try again. Which trait is this?
r: Resilience
The person recovers and adapts.

q: What is an entrepreneur's role in the economy?
r: Creating new businesses, jobs and ideas
Entrepreneurs drive innovation.

q: What is start-up capital?
r: The money needed to start a business
It pays for equipment and supplies.
w: The profit earned in the first year
The tax paid by a new business

q: What is bootstrapping?
r: Starting a business with little outside money, mostly personal savings
The owner funds growth from earnings.
w: Selling a business to a competitor

q: Which is a typical source of funding for a start-up that wants to keep full ownership?
r: Personal savings or a bank loan
Owners keep their shares.
w: Selling a large share of the company
Giving investors half of future profits forever

q: What is a business model?
r: How a business creates, delivers and earns money from value
It explains how the business works.
w: A small version of a product
A person who advertises a product
A building where products are made

q: A start-up gives away a free app and earns money from ads. What is this?
r: A business model that earns revenue from advertising
The app is free to users.
w: A nonprofit model with no revenue
A subscription model charging monthly fees

q: What is a minimum viable product (MVP)?
r: A basic version of a product used to test an idea with real users
It saves time and money.
w: The final perfect version of a product
A product that has no features
A product sold only to investors

q: What is a pitch?
r: A short presentation that explains a business idea to investors or customers
It aims to persuade.

q: What should an investor pitch always include?
r: The problem, the solution, the market and how the business makes money
Investors need these to judge the idea.
w: Only the color of the logo
Only a list of competitors' names

q: What is scaling a business?
r: Growing revenue faster than costs
It means serving more customers efficiently.
w: Keeping the business exactly the same size

q: Which is a risk of growing too fast?
r: Running out of cash or being unable to meet demand
Growth must be supported.
w: Having too many satisfied customers to count

q: What is liquidity?
r: How easily an asset can be turned into cash
Cash is the most liquid asset.
w: How much profit a business earns
How much debt a business owes
How long a business has operated

q: Which ratio best measures a firm's ability to pay short-term debts?
r: The current ratio
It compares current assets to current liabilities.
w: It measures how fast stock sells.

q: What is return on investment (ROI)?
r: The gain from an investment relative to its cost
It is usually shown as a percent.
w: The time needed to repay a loan

q: A business spends $20,000 on equipment and earns an extra $3,000 profit a year from it. What is the annual ROI?
r: $3,000 divided by $20,000 equals 0.15.

q: What is working capital?
r: Current assets minus current liabilities
It shows short-term financial health.

q: What does a debt ratio measure?
r: The share of assets financed by debt
It is total liabilities divided by total assets.
w: The share of sales kept as profit
How much cash is on hand

q: Liabilities are $60,000 and assets are $150,000. What is the debt ratio?
r: $60,000 divided by $150,000 equals 0.40.

q: What is inventory turnover?
r: How many times inventory is sold and replaced in a period
It is cost of goods sold divided by average inventory.
w: The number of products in a warehouse

q: Cost of goods sold is $240,000 and average inventory is $40,000. What is inventory turnover?
r: 6 times
$240,000 divided by $40,000 equals 6.

q: What is recruitment?
r: Finding and attracting qualified candidates for jobs
It begins the hiring process.

q: Which interview question is unlawful to ask?
r: Are you planning to have children?
Family plans can lead to discrimination.
w: Can you perform the essential job duties?
Are you legally allowed to work here?
Why are you interested in this job?

q: What is a performance appraisal?
r: A formal review of an employee's work
It guides feedback and development.
w: A review of the office layout

q: What is employee turnover?
r: The rate at which employees leave and are replaced
High turnover is costly.
w: The rate at which sales grow
The rate at which profits rise

q: A company with 150 employees sees 30 leave in a year. What is the turnover rate?
r: 30 divided by 150 equals 0.20.

q: What is job rotation?
r: Moving employees between different jobs to build skills
It reduces boredom.
w: Keeping staff in one job forever

q: What is diversity in the workplace?
r: Differences among employees such as background and experience
Diverse teams bring varied ideas.
w: Having every employee do the same task
Hiring only people of one age

q: What is a grievance procedure?
r: A fair process for employees to raise and resolve complaints
It protects employees' rights.
w: A way to fire workers without notice
That is not a procedure for complaints.

q: What is a spreadsheet used for?
r: Organizing and calculating data in rows and columns
Formulas update results automatically.

q: Which spreadsheet function adds a column of numbers?
r: SUM
=SUM(A1:A10) adds ten cells.

q: What is data backup?
r: Making copies of data to restore it if the original is lost
It protects against loss.

q: What is phishing?
r: A scam that tricks people into revealing sensitive information
It often uses fake emails.
w: That is not the tech meaning.

q: An email asks you to confirm your password on an unfamiliar link. What should you do?
r: Not click and report it
It is likely phishing.

q: What is cloud computing?
r: Using remote servers on the internet to store and process data
Services are used on demand.
w: Using only one computer in an office

q: What is a target market?
r: The specific group of customers a business aims to serve
Focus improves results.

q: A company sells running shoes mainly to serious athletes. What is this?
r: Target marketing
It focuses on a chosen group.

q: What is branding?
r: Creating a name or symbol that identifies a business's products
Brands build recognition.

q: What is market research?
r: Gathering information about customers and competitors
It guides decisions.

q: What is supply chain management?
r: Coordinating the flow of goods from suppliers to customers
It aims to deliver on time at low cost.

q: A factory runs short of a key part because one supplier is late. What is the best long-term fix?
r: Use more than one supplier
Backups reduce dependence.
w: Rely on the same single supplier

q: What is quality control?
r: Checking products to ensure they meet standards
It catches defects.

q: What is a professional network?
r: A group of contacts who share advice and opportunities
Networking helps careers.
w: A computer network inside an office

q: Which action best shows professionalism after making a mistake at work?
r: Admit it, fix it and learn from it
It shows accountability.
w: Hide it and hope no one notices

q: What is a competitive advantage?
r: A strength that lets a business outperform rivals
It might be lower cost or better service.
w: A law that blocks rival businesses
A tax paid by all businesses

q: A small bakery cannot beat a chain on price but offers fresh, local products. What strategy is it using?
r: Differentiation
It stands out on quality and uniqueness.
w: It is choosing a different approach.
